subject.title: feat(workspace): add tiered bootstrap loading with configurable bootstrapTier

question: Should OpenClaw accept `agents.defaults.bootstrapTier` as a core config surface now, and if so should no-override defaults preserve existing `bootstrap-extra-files` behavior?
rationale: The implementation is a bounded feature, but it changes public config, prompt context selection, and existing hook-extra behavior in ways automation should not decide without maintainer intent.

options.title: Preserve compatibility and continue review
options.body: Keep the new config shape under review, but require the no-override path to behave like current main and add public docs before merge.

options.title: Accept a breaking default cleanup
options.body: Maintainers may intentionally drop hook extras from no-override subagent and cron sessions, but that needs explicit upgrade notes and proof rather than an implicit compatibility claim.

options.title: Fold into broader context-control design
options.body: Pause or close this PR if maintainers want tiering handled together with broader bootstrap selection and prompt-pressure proposals.

recommendation.title: Preserve compatibility and continue review
recommendation.body: Keep the new config shape under review, but require the no-override path to behave like current main and add public docs before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Prior review context and adjacent bootstrap ownership make this the clearest owner for the API/defaults decision.
